reason: The cited evidence (E1) shows Cu-rich phase melting on the surface of a bulk CoCrCu alloy at ~1100 °C, supporting the idea that Cu can segregate and melt first. However, it does not address nanoparticles, sluggish diffusion kinetics, or the formation of a liquid-like shell, leaving most key premises unsupported by the provided evidence.
premises: Cu has a lower melting point than the other elements in the HEA
Cu will preferentially segregate to the nanoparticle surface upon heating
Sluggish diffusion kinetics in HEAs facilitate this segregation
The segregated Cu forms a liquid-like shell that initiates premelting
This surface premelting precedes bulk melting
